\begin{document}
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:base}
The base case holds for $n=1$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Direct substitution.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:step}
The inductive step holds.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Assume the claim for $n$; a short computation gives $n+1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:all}
The identity holds for all $n$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
By \cref{lem:base} and \Cref{lem:step}, induction closes the argument.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:top}
The generating function is rational.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\cref{cor:all} gives the identity, and Lemma 2 supplies the recursion.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
